footnotes.c: See Table 8 for definition of the PE severity and PE-related risk.
footnotes.d: Dabigatran is not recommended in patients with CrCl <30 mL/min. Edoxaban should be given at a dose of 30 mg once daily in patients with CrCl of 15–50 mL/min and is not recommended in patients with CrCl <15 mL/min. Rivaroxaban and apixaban are to be used with caution in patients with CrCl 15–29 mL/min, and their use is not recommended in patients with CrCl <15 mL/min.
footnotes.e: If appropriate expertise and resources are available on-site.
footnotes.f: The risk-to-benefit ratios of surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed procedures have not yet been established in intermediate- or low-risk PE.

content.section_heading: 6.8 Recommendations for multidisciplinary pulmonary embolism teams

recommendation_summary.text: Set-up of a multidisciplinary team and a programme for the management of high- and (in selected cases) intermediate-risk PE should be considered, depending on the resources and expertise available in each hospital.
recommendation_summary.note: Recommendation box is shown twice in the image (duplicate).

content.other_notes: Reference to Table 8 for PE severity. Emphasis on renal function (CrCl) for DOAC use and dosing; several direct oral anticoagulants named (dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban, apixaban).
